answers.brief_reasoning: More UV causes more mutations, so more resistant mutants are expected.
answers.final_answer: As UV exposure time increases, the number of colonies on the antibiotic plates will increase. There should be few or no colonies at 0 s.

answers.brief_reasoning: UV damages DNA, causing mutations; longer exposure gives more mutations, so it is more likely that some cells gain a resistance mutation.
answers.final_answer: UV light damages DNA, for example by forming thymine dimers, and errors in repairing this damage create mutations. Longer exposure causes more DNA damage and mutations, so it is more likely that some cells get a mutation that makes them resistant to the antibiotic. Those cells survive and form colonies.

answers.brief_reasoning: Homologs synapse to form tetrads; non-sister chromatids exchange corresponding segments at chiasmata.
answers.final_answer: Homologous chromosomes pair up (synapsis) to form a tetrad. Non-sister chromatids then exchange matching segments of DNA at chiasmata, so alleles are swapped between the maternal and paternal homologs.

answers.brief_reasoning: Recombinant chromatids carry new allele combinations.
answers.final_answer: Crossing over produces recombinant chromatids that carry new combinations of the maternal and paternal alleles of linked genes. These combinations were not present on either parental chromosome, so the four products of meiosis differ from each other and from the parent's chromosomes, which increases the number of different possible gametes.

answers.brief_reasoning: Loss of recombination reduces variation; independent assortment remains.
answers.final_answer: Genetic variation among the gametes will decrease. Some variation remains because the two chromosome pairs still assort independently, giving 2^2 = 4 chromosome combinations.

answers.brief_reasoning: Chromosomes keep parental allele combinations.
answers.final_answer: Without crossing over, each chromosome passed to a gamete keeps exactly the same combination of alleles it had in the parent (all maternal or all paternal), so linked alleles are always inherited together. The gametes can therefore only carry one of the 4 combinations of whole parental chromosomes produced by independent assortment, with no recombinant chromosomes.

answers.brief_reasoning: Definition
answers.final_answer: Genetic drift is a random change in allele frequencies in a population from one generation to the next. It comes from chance events, such as which individuals happen to survive and reproduce, and not from natural selection.

answers.brief_reasoning: Sampling error
answers.final_answer: In a small population, each individual makes up a large share of the gene pool. Chance events (sampling error) can therefore change allele frequencies a lot and can even make an allele disappear. In a large population, random gains and losses tend to cancel out, so the frequencies stay closer to what they were.

answers.brief_reasoning: Bottleneck lowers allelic diversity
answers.final_answer: The recovered population of 5,000 will have fewer different alleles of the gene than the original population did, even though it is back to the same size.

answers.brief_reasoning: Survivors carry limited alleles
answers.final_answer: The 20 survivors carry at most 40 copies of each gene, and these are a random sample of the original gene pool. Rare alleles were probably not carried by any survivor, so they were lost. The recovered population comes only from the survivors' alleles, and new alleles from mutation build up very slowly, so the lost alleles do not come back.

answers.brief_reasoning: Competition definition
answers.final_answer: Competition is an interaction in which two species use the same limited resource (e.g., space, food), so each one reduces the resource available to the other. This lowers the growth, survival or reproduction of both (a -/- interaction).

answers.brief_reasoning: Predation lowers prey numbers
answers.final_answer: The sea star eats mussels, so it raises the mussels' death rate. This keeps the mussel population smaller than it would be without the predator, below the size where mussels could cover all the rock space.

answers.brief_reasoning: Keystone predator removed
answers.final_answer: The number of species living on the rocks will decrease where the sea stars were removed, compared with the unchanged area.

answers.brief_reasoning: Competitive exclusion
answers.final_answer: With no sea stars eating them, mussels grow in number and spread over the rock surface. Because mussels are the strongest competitor for space, they take over the limited space and crowd out the other species (competitive exclusion). Those species can no longer attach or survive there, so diversity drops. This shows the sea star is a keystone predator.

answers.brief_reasoning: Homologs fail to separate in meiosis I, or sister chromatids fail to separate in meiosis II. One daughter cell gets an extra chromosome (n+1) and another is missing one (n−1), so the egg is aneuploid.
answers.final_answer: Nondisjunction means chromosomes fail to separate during meiosis I or II. The egg ends up with an extra or missing chromosome (n+1 or n−1), which leads to trisomy or monosomy after fertilization.

difficulty.rationale: Four-part short FR on a single small table. Part A asks for a trend description with supporting values. Part B is one percent-change calculation with clean numbers, (3 months - 18 months)/18 months, about -93.2%. Part C compares mean ± 2SE ranges: 18 months is 24.64-31.16, 12 months is 8.1-9.7, and 3 months is 1.7-2.1, so the ranges do not overlap and the claim is supported. Part D asks for an explanation of nondisjunction producing an abnormal chromosome number. All levers are allowed (table reading, one formula-sheet calculation, 2SE comparison, a disruption in meiosis). Reading load is light, the arithmetic is short, and the context is concrete and unambiguous. The depth is typical AP exam level and not above it, so it fits a full mock.
